audience.text: Developers building .NET applications that require 3D scene construction, manipulation, and format conversion without native dependencies.

capabilities.text: Build and traverse 3D scene graphs using Scene and Node classes, with support for child node attachment and entity assignment.
capabilities.title: Construct 3D scene graphs

capabilities.text: Generate primitive shapes like Box, Cylinder, Sphere, and IFC-compatible 2D profiles such as LShape, TShape, and RectangleShape.
capabilities.title: Create primitive and CAD-style geometry

capabilities.text: Attach materials including LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, and PbrMaterial to nodes using PbrMaterial.FromMaterial() for conversion.
capabilities.title: Assign shading materials

capabilities.text: Read and write FBX, glTF, Wavefront OBJ, STL, COLLADA, U3D, 3MF, RVM, AMF, and HTML5/Aspose 3D Web viewer exports.
capabilities.title: Convert between interchange formats

capabilities.text: Support for AnimationClip, AnimationChannel, KeyFrame, Bone, Skeleton, SkinDeformer, and MorphTargetDeformer.
capabilities.title: Animate scenes with keyframes

capabilities.text: Create NurbsCurve and NurbsSurface objects with control points, weights, and knot vectors.
capabilities.title: Define NURBS curves and surfaces

capabilities.text: Read and write per-vertex attributes including normals, UVs, vertex color, tangent/binormal, and user data via VertexDeclaration.
capabilities.title: Access per-vertex mesh data

limitations.text: Rendering is not implemented — Scene.Render, RenderFactory, and IRenderTarget/IRenderWindow throw NotImplementedException.
PolygonModifier and most TriMesh helpers throw NotImplementedException — mesh post-processing utilities beyond basic scene-graph construction are not functional.
NURBS evaluation and conversion to mesh via NurbsCurve.Evaluate and NurbsSurface.ToMesh throw NotImplementedException.
PLY import/export works via Scene.Open/Save but direct use of FileFormat.PLY throws NotImplementedException.
PDF and Google Draco import/export are not functional — no reader/writer implementation exists.
License and Metered APIs exist for API compatibility but are not applicable to this open-source edition.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic 3D scene creation and conversion using pure managed code with no native dependencies.
Supports round-trip conversion between widely used 3D interchange formats including FBX, glTF, OBJ, STL, COLLADA, and U3D.
Provides a consistent API surface compatible with Aspose.3D for .NET Enterprise Edition for migration and compatibility.

product_summary.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for .NET is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed .NET library for building, traversing, and converting 3D scenes without external 3D engines.

uncertainties: The exact set of supported 3D formats beyond those explicitly mentioned in examples and limitations is not fully enumerated.
Whether PLY format support via Scene.Open/Save is complete or partial (e.g., vertex-only vs. full material/texture support) is not specified.
The behavior of Scene.Open() when encountering malformed or partially corrupted files beyond unrecognized extensions is not documented.
Whether animation data (e.g., keyframes, bones) round-trips correctly across all supported formats is not confirmed by examples.

workflows.name: Load and convert scenes
workflows.text: Load a 3D scene from a file using Scene.FromFile() and save it to another format using Scene.Save() with appropriate FileFormat constants.

workflows.name: Build scenes from primitives
workflows.text: Construct a new Scene, add primitive entities like Box or Cylinder via Node.CreateChildNode(), and save the result to formats like FBX or COLLADA.

workflows.name: Configure format-specific options
workflows.text: Use dedicated load/save options types such as ObjLoadOptions to control coordinate system flipping and normal normalization during import/export.

workflows.name: Handle unrecognized formats
workflows.text: Catch ArgumentException when Scene.Open() fails to resolve a FileFormat for an unknown file extension.
